title: ThreadLocal Memory Leaks in Pooled Executors

spark.summary: Understand how ThreadLocalMap strong value references pin memory on long-lived pool threads and cause cross-request context bleed.
spark.keyTakeaway: When input scale outgrows single-pass linear memory, always pair ThreadLocal.set() with finally { remove(); } or use ScopedValue.
spark.byteSummary: In Java ThreadLocalMap, the key is a WeakReference but the Entry value is a strong reference. Because worker threads in HTTP pools never terminate, omitted remove() calls pin O(T x M) heap permanently and expose stale tenant state to subsequent requests.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement ThreadLocal Memory Leaks in Pooled Executors without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When input scale outgrows single-pass linear memory, always pair ThreadLocal.set() with finally { remove(); } or use ScopedValue.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.
